This page is a work log, not a second report. Short bullets are welcome. It is separate from the final case study and does not count toward the 750 to 1,000 word range.

## Starting point

**AI system and date:** Gemini, Nov 6, 2026

**Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.** 
Research Question: To what extent do nutritional components (total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, sodium, carbs, fiber, sugar, protein) and restaurant chain predict the cholesterol content in fast-food menu items?

Baseline Model: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple linear regression predicting cholesterol from nutritional macronutrients and restaurant indicators.

Limitation of Baseline: Linear regression assumes additive, straight-line relationships between nutrients and cholesterol. It struggles to capture non-linear patterns and complex multi-way interactions (for instance, the joint effect of high sodium and saturated fat on cholesterol within fried items versus grilled items).

## Substantive prompts

Paste the exact prompts that shaped the extension. Include the customized extension-selection prompt from the checkpoint and any important implementation follow-ups. Delete unused prompt blocks.

> We are analyzing a fast-food nutrition dataset to predict cholesterol using multiple linear regression with predictors like total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, sodium, carbs, sugars, protein, and restaurant brand. Our baseline model shows reasonable fit ($R^2$), but residual diagnostics suggest non-linearities and potential interaction effects that linear regression cannot easily capture. Propose an advanced beyond-course machine learning extension to compare against our baseline, provide the implementation steps, and explain how to evaluate it against the linear model.

## My decisions

- **Accepted:** We will use a Random Forest Regressor as a non-parametric benchmark to capture non-linearities and multi-nutrient interactions that linear models struggle with.
- **Changed:** We limited the predictors (total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, sodium, carbs, fiber, sugar, protein) and restaurant brand, rather than letting the AI include redundant items like total calories or item names.
- **Rejected or corrected:** Rejected overly complex hyperparameter tuning suggestions

**Connection to the final case study:** The Random Forest methods will be integrated into the Model Comparison and Advanced Analysis section of our final report, It will serve as a useful comparison to an OLS model.
## Independent verification

1. **Check and result:** 5-Fold Cross-Validation Metric Comparison: We will evaluate both the baseline linear regression and the Random Forest model using the exact same 5-fold cross-validation splits.

2. **Check and result:** We will plot predicted values versus residuals for the Random Forest to ensure residuals are randomly distributed around zero and do not display systematic bias.

## Remaining limitation

**State one important uncertainty, failure mode, or limitation that remains.** While the Random Forest model may fit the line better, it will sacrifice the simplicity and easy interpretation of variable coefficients that show how just one predictor can affect the model.

## Other AI use, if any

We heavily used AI to fix issues with setting up our github, as well as briefly asking it to clarify certain requirements on the project. Before our initial prompt, we asked for 5 different options that were beyond the scope of this class so that we could choose which best added to our model.
